newsitem.title: USA: Housing starts up modestly in June, signs of leveling seen.
newsitem.headline: Housing starts up modestly in June, signs of leveling seen.

text.p: Construction starts on new homes and apartments rose modestly in June, the Commerce Department said on Thursday, as building began to show signs of leveling off from a hot pace earlier this year.

Total starts increased 4.8 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.45 million in June. That followed a revised 6.6 percent drop in May to 1.39 million, which was previously reported as a 4.8 percent decline.

With mortgage rates relatively low and falling, the housing market remains solid in terms of both building and sales, though it is off the peaks it hit in late winter when unusually warm weather fostered a boom in construction.
Last month's building rate was down 2.4 percent from June 1996, when construction was taking place at a rate of 1.49 million new homes a year.

As well, applications for new building permits declined in June by 2.6 percent to an annual rate of 1.40 million -- a third straight monthly decline that brought applications back to the same level prevailing at the end of last year.
The building industry has predicted a leveling off of construction activity as the year wears on.
The National Association of Home Builders said on Wednesday that its index of market activity was unchanged in July at 57, the same as in June.

"Overall, the housing market appears stable and healthy," said Kent Colton, executive vice president of the builders' lobby group. But he added the likelihood was for "a gradual slowing of the market and a slight decline in housing starts for the year."

Construction starts on single-family homes rose in June by 2.6 percent to a rate of 1.11 million after falling 4.5 percent in May. Starts on apartments increased 12.9 percent to a rate of 342,000, largely retracing a 13.4 percent plunge in May.

Mortage rates eased in June from May. The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp., or Freddie Mac, said rates for a 30-year loan averaged 7.69 percent in June, down from 7.94 percent in May. Rates have fallen further in July.

Regionally, starts jumped 11.2 percent in the South, the nation's largest regional housing market, to 683,000 a year. They increased 1.1 percent in the West to 362,000 and were up 0.7 percent to a rate of 294,000 in the Midwest.
The only region where starts actually declined in June was in the Northeast, where they fell by 6.6 percent to 113,000.
